answer: Because the signal stake is held until the vault settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the spiral audit lists each exposure. A farm running 111 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. An attester must stake 49% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. That is 12 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
